Author:     Max Engel <max@awecelot.com>
AuthorDate: Thu Sep 10 23:41:39 2026 +0000
Commit:     Max Engel <max@awecelot.com>
CommitDate: Thu Sep 10 23:41:39 2026 +0000

    Add a unit-test binary for the pure cloud text
    
    #120 box 4: the cheapest test this project can run. 19 cases, 162
    assertions, four thousandths of a second, and no image, no VM and no
    device between writing a parser and knowing what it does with junk.
    
    What is covered is what nobody types twice: every ">>> " shape the
    scripts print, including a line missing its field, a why with a
    trailing full stop, the transfer page's markers this reader must not
    claim, and a line that only looks like one; each stamp shape both
    writers emit, plus an empty file, a one-field file, an epoch of zero
    and bytes that are not a stamp at all; the ten-second window that makes
    two stamps the same run, at 10 and at 11 either side; D-UI-035's worked
    example shortening to three candidate lines; a hostname with spaces,
    with UTF-8, with hyphens at both ends, at 70 characters and at the
    truncation that would leave a trailing hyphen.
    
    Proved to fail before it was trusted: widening the origin window to 11,
    the hostname limit to 64, and shortenWhy's dash to " -- " fails 3 cases
    and 7 assertions; reverting them passes again.
    
    doctest 2.4.12 as a single header in external/doctest, the latest of
    the 2.4 line. The target is es-unit-tests, behind ES_BUILD_TESTS
    (default OFF, so an image build never builds or links it), and
    es-app/tests/unit/CMakeLists.txt stands on its own as well -- which is
    how it is meant to be run, since the top-level CMakeLists cannot
    configure on a host without SDL, OpenGL, freetype and curl. The binary
    compiles the tests, CloudText.cpp and StringUtil.cpp, and nothing else
    of EmulationStation.
    
    The i18n target's xgettext runs over all of es-app, so the tests are in
    its path: they are pure ASCII and carry no _(), and the sweep over the
    tree is clean.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
